question: Whether profit-to-cash realization and net-share change can be distinguished from existing gross-profit/assets and operating-cash/assets using the eight fixed value-source cases

conclusion.profit_cash: Existing P2 fields include consolidated revenue, operating cost, total assets and operating cash flow, but no qualified net-profit field. Gross profit is revenue minus cost, not net profit. Therefore net profit minus operating cash cannot be reconstructed by renaming GP/CFO. Five fixed PDFs visibly contain both consolidated total net profit and parent-attributable net profit, which differ, so a new definition must choose the numerator, bind announcement/version and qualify the exact consolidated statement before any comparison. It may still be a transformation of profit and cash rather than independent information.
conclusion.net_shares: A year-end share count difference is not equivalent to cash financing. The fixed originals show cash placement, A/H shares, employee incentives, repurchase cancellation and bonus shares. Cash financing would need event-level amount, consideration, date, share class, registration, treasury/cancellation and financing-cash-flow reconciliation; one annual count or share-capital line cannot establish it.
conclusion.decision: P4 is source-feasible in five examples only; no 600-company eligible panel, performance result, real trading rule or ETF transfer is established. Continue profit-cash as a quality-family source question; keep net-share/cash-financing as a separate source candidate pending event evidence.

missing_for_profit_cash: qualified consolidated total net profit or explicitly chosen parent-attributable net profit
same-fiscal-year and same-report-version income and cash-flow fields
receivables/inventory and other accrual components for explanation
same-scale denominator and prior-year persistence if claimed
existing_input_boundary.existing_p2_cfo_caveat: CFO/assets is one annual cash-flow level divided by end assets; it does not already measure accruals, income-to-cash conversion or persistence.

shares.evidence: Private A-share placement of 1,578,947,368 shares at RMB3.80/share; report states RMB5,999,999,998.40 raised and total shares rose to 8,002,591,027. Financing cash flow also records investment cash received on page 45, but event-to-cash reconciliation and use-of-proceeds still require checking.

Report describes both listed A and H shares and 1,658,610,000 total year-end shares; year-end share capital line is unchanged from previous year on page 101. A-only price cannot value or interpret all classes.

Two 2024 restricted-share incentive vestings changed total shares from 1,113,738,857 to 1,116,163,857 and then 1,116,701,357; share-capital line on page 86 reflects the final count. The count increase alone does not say whether ordinary outside investors supplied cash.

Report describes repurchase and cancellation of 480,000 incentive shares and registration of 27,510,000 restricted shares; year-end shares reached 4,974,253,675. Page 101 separately shows treasury stock and other equity instruments. Gross share change combines distinct events, so cannot be read as net cash financing.

Implementation of the prior annual distribution gave one bonus share per ten existing shares and increased total shares by 103,818,000 to 1,141,998,000. This is a direct counterexample to treating positive share-count change as cash raised; the same section says no new securities issuance/listing in the recent three years.

unresolved: The five visible values have not been promoted to a frozen historical net-profit panel; report dates and correction coverage beyond these original PDFs remain unqualified.

For total-versus-parent profit, the appropriate financial object and alignment with consolidated CFO must be frozen before testing; minority interests explain why the numbers differ but do not by themselves select a formula.
Operating cash can diverge from net profit through working capital, taxes, noncash costs and timing; five examples do not establish future risk or returns.

Share-count comparability requires splits, bonus shares, A/H classes, restricted shares, repurchases held as treasury versus cancelled, corporate actions and actual cash received/paid. Cash-flow statement line items alone may aggregate multiple events.
P4 has no new source requests, effect tests, ETF evidence, account outcomes or production authority.
